A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same EMOVA research work with complete, readable main text and appendices A–G. Full-text and rendered-page comparisons establish that differences are confined to the first-page author list and version/date stamp.

before.justification: v1 reports original EMOVA benchmark results, spoken-dialogue evaluations, and ablations in Tables 3–4 and 6–7 and Figures 2 and 7.

after.justification: v2 retains the original EMOVA benchmark results, spoken-dialogue evaluations, and ablations in Tables 3–4 and 6–7 and Figures 2 and 7.

M1.justification: Sections 3–4 and Appendices A–B retain identical architecture, speech tokenization, style control, alignment, training, and response-generation procedures.

E1.justification: Training datasets, the 14 vision-language benchmarks, English and Chinese speech evaluations, and qualitative test scenarios are unchanged, including all appendix coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in Tables 3 and 6, including Mini-Omni, AnyGPT, and VITA. The alignment comparisons in Figure 2 also retain the same alternatives.

E3.justification: Table 2, Sections 4–5, and Appendices B–E preserve the same training settings, dataset splits, sample counts, metrics, and evaluation procedures.

E4.justification: The alignment and disentanglement comparisons in Figure 2, emotion-control analysis in Figure 7, vision-configuration ablations in Table 7, and Appendix G case studies are identical.

E5.justification: Both versions use the same point estimates and averaging procedures. Neither adds repeated-run or seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical results and qualitative examples are identical. For example, Table 6 retains EMOVA's LibriSpeech WER of 4.0 and TTS-WER of 3.4, and AISHELL-2 CER of 10.3 and TTS-CER of 7.9.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(2), token and vocabulary definitions, and the chain-of-modality factorization are identical. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's three contributions, and conclusion retain identical claims about joint alignment, emotional speech control, and simultaneous state-of-the-art vision-language and speech performance.

C2.justification: Result interpretations remain identical, including explanations of alignment benefits and speech-recognition errors. Appendix F retains the same limitations concerning duplex modeling, direct unit-to-unit generation, and vision configurations.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, data preparation, and evaluation prompts are unchanged. The project-page disclosure and PDF hyperlink targets are also identical.

R1.justification: Section 2, comparisons with prior work throughout the appendices, and the bibliography are identical. No citations or research-positioning claims are added or removed.

P1.justification: v2 adds Jun Yao to the author list and updates the arXiv version/date stamp from v1, 26 September 2024, to v2, 29 October 2024. All substantive prose and document organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–25, Tables 1–7, captions, and placements are unchanged. Pages 2–35 render identically, while page 1 retains its layout despite the author and stamp text updates.

improvement.justification: The only changes are the added author and updated version/date stamp. Scientific content, empirical evidence, reproducibility information, limitations, and presentation remain unchanged throughout the main text and appendices, establishing no meaningful difference in overall paper quality.
